answer: An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the garden index resolves every citation against the basalt checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the quill audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 206 aliases hence burns the authoring cost 206 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 27 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
